assertions.evidence: @TableTest annotations appear on both methods: `@TableTest("""...Scenario | Input | Expected?...""")`

assertions.text: Null input is represented as a blank cell in the valid inputs @TableTest table (not the string 'null', and not as a separate @Test method). The blank cell maps to a null parameter.
assertions.evidence: In the first table: `Null input      |        |` shows blank cells for both Input and Expected columns. The response explains: 'blank cell → `null` parameter' and '`assertEquals(null, null)` passes when `parse(null)` returns null'

assertions.text: The exception/invalid-input table has an expected column (e.g. 'Throws?' or 'Exception?') specifying the exception type per row — rather than hardcoding the exception type in @Description or the method name.
assertions.evidence: Second table includes column `Throws?` with rows: `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` (three times), providing the exception type per row

assertions.text: The exception cases (empty string, letters-only, negative) are handled — via a Throws? column, assertThrows in the method body, or a separate @TableTest — not silently omitted
assertions.evidence: Second @TableTest covers all three cases: `Empty string | '' | java.lang.IllegalArgumentException`, `Letters only | abc | java.lang.IllegalArgumentException`, `Negative value | -5.00 | java.lang.IllegalArgumentException` with `assertThrows(throws_, () -> parse(input));`

assertions.text: Valid inputs have a result column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Money?' or 'Result?')

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: First method body: `assertEquals(expected, parse(input));` and second method body: `assertThrows(throws_, () -> parse(input));` — neither contains if or switch

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case (e.g. 'moneyParsing' → 'Money Parsing'). Not a generic name like 'test1' or 'testMethod'.
assertions.evidence: Method names are descriptive: `shouldParseInput` (converts to 'Should Parse Input') and `shouldRejectInvalidInput` (converts to 'Should Reject Invalid Input')

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as the expected currency format, or open questions. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show. It is acceptable to omit @Description if the table already conveys all relevant context.
assertions.evidence: No @Description annotations are present in the code, which is acceptable per the assertion rule: 'It is acceptable to omit @Description if the table already conveys all relevant context'

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Both methods have only @TableTest annotations (no @DisplayName or @Description), so the order is correct
